ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each UBO, director, legal representative, and significant shareholder against (i) the SAGRILAFT risk matrix administrator under Circular Externa 004 de 2019; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) EU autonomous sanctions where applicable; (v) Colombia's UIAF consolidated PEP list; and (vi) local judicial and disciplinary records via the Procuraduría and Consejo de Estado. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to PEPs, including senior-compliance-officer approval, source-of-funds verification, and transaction-history inspection. Periodic rescreening is required every six months or upon any material change in ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (www.rues.org.co); name search and reservation are initiated through the online portal of the territorial Cámara de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must be expressed in Spanish or in an admitted Latin-script transliteration; foreign-language names must include a Spanish distinctive phrase or body and must be easily recognizable in the local language. The corporate name must contain 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' or the abbreviation 'S.A.S.' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name, trademark, or famous designation. Accents, prepositions, articles, and the conjunction 'y' are disregarded for comparative purposes; phonetically and visually similar names are assessed in the same economic sector.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name, the applicant has 10 business days from notification to file a 'recurso de reposición' directly with the Cámara de Comercio, setting out factual and legal grounds for reversal. The Cámara has 30 business days to decide; if the rejection is upheld, the applicant may file an 'apelación' to the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the same appeal period. Exhaustion of these administrative remedies permits judicial review before the Cámara de la Jurisdicción Contencioso-Administrativa within 4 months of final adverse decision. There is no statutory extension of the 30-day reservation window; after expiration the applicant must submit a new request or reserve an alternative name to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office acceptance is limited: for statutory residence and administrative service of process, a Cámara de Comercio-recognized virtual office may be tolerated; however, a physical and operational establishment is mandatory for cold-chain keg wholesale and distribution, requiring municipal zoning approval, INVIMA sanitary licensing for alcohol and food handling, and DIAN customs/excise tax registration. The commercial and fiscal address must reflect the physical warehouse or distribution facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 70.0% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months of operation, driven by INVIMA sanitary controls, DIAN excise/customs risk profiling, and local municipal health and zoning inspections for alcohol-beverage distributors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada) as amended; Código de Comercio de Colombia (Decree 410 of 1971), Book II, Title IV, arts. 98–151, and arts. 372–460 on commercial registers; Decreto 898 de 2019 regulating administrative procedure before the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the company's registered office, acting through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) and the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation deed); if real property is contributed, formalization by public deed before a Notary Public is required before registry filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required. The subscribed and paid capital is freely determined in the bylaws. If the bylaws are silent, at least one-third of the value of each subscribed share must be paid at the time of constitution and the balance within one year (Código de Comercio, art. 126). Contributions may be evidenced by bank receipt or asset delivery and must be reflected in the registry file.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a duly convened first meeting of the founding shareholders, the following resolutions were approved unanimously: (1) the articles of incorporation of [Company] S.A.S. are adopted, and the subscribed capital of COP [capital] is issued to the founding shareholders; (2) the registered office is fixed at [address], Municipality of [city], Department of [department], Colombia, for all legal and administrative purposes; (3) [Name] is appointed Legal Representative and [Name] is appointed Substitute Legal Representative, with the powers set forth in Article 10 of Law 1258 of 2008; and (4) the Legal Representative is authorized to complete all filings with the Chamber of Commerce and other public authorities. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Validation and Homonymy Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio / RUES electronic window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a homonymy certificate request through the RUES portal or at the Chamber of Commerce customer service window to verify that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered business. The certificate of name availability is valid for 90 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Solicitud de certificado de homonimia
Identity document of the requesting incorporator
Proposed corporate name and economic activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or registry conflict, refile a new homonymy request with a distinctive name modifier or abbreviation; correct the proposed company name and re-submit without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Execution of the Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders with optional notarization at a Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Documento Privado de Constitución containing clauses on corporate scope, subscribed and paid capital, governance, board composition, legal representation, audit committee (if any), tax domicile, and liquidation mechanism. If the company receives real estate as capital contribution, the instrument must be elevated to a public deed before a Notary Public.
required_dossiers: Documento Privado de Constitución (bylaws)
Certificado de homonimia
Passport or national identity card of each incorporator
Power of attorney if an incorporator is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies legal or formal omissions, correct the instrument, obtain the missing signatures, and re-execute before the relevant authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registry Registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation instrument and supporting forms to the Chamber of Commerce with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. Pay the registration fee calculated on the subscribed capital. Upon successful registration, the Chamber issues the official Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal evidencing the company's existence and legal representative's powers.
required_dossiers: Documento Privado de Constitución (original and copy)
Certificado de homonimia
Formulario RUES de matrícula mercantil
Pre-RUT fiscal information sheet
Identification documents of shareholders and officers
Receipt of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber files a corrective notice, address the objections within the stated period, pay any outstanding jurisdiction fees, amend the instrument, and re-submit for a final endorsement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Identification and Activation at DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the pre-RUT file generated during the commercial registration, complete the electronic RUT form on the DIAN portal to obtain the definitive NIT. Ensure the socioeconomic and fiscal responsibilities are correctly flagged, including income tax, VAT, and industry and commerce register codes as applicable.
required_dossiers: Pre-RUT electronic record
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Identity document of the legal representative
Lease or ownership title confirming fiscal domicile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or requires clarification, correct the RUT data and re-submit; if the NIT is already assigned but the RUT contains errors, file an update through RUES or the DIAN virtual office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Capital Payment Acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank of company's choice (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda, Citibank Colombia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in Colombia to hold the company's cash contributions and operational funds. Deposit the paid-in capital and obtain a bank certificate or receipt evidencing the deposit. This receipt may be required to complete the Chamber of Commerce registration file and to validate the paid-in portion of subscribed capital.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (not older than 3 months)
Articles of incorporation and bylaws
RUT assigned by DIAN
Identification documents of shareholders and legal representative
AML/KYC compliance forms of the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional corporate or beneficial-ownership documentation, provide the required information or restructure the application; the legal representative may also appoint the bank as a reporting agent for tax purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commencement of Activities Notice and Municipal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN and the local municipal finance or planning authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal commencement-of-activities notice to DIAN and register the company with the municipal tax and planning office for industry and trade tax (ICA) and any zoning, signage, and operational permits. Ensure the registered activity code matches ISIC 4632 for wholesale distribution.
required_dossiers: Definitive RUT with commercial activity code
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Municipal business registration form
Lease or ownership contract for the warehouse, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or DIAN reports incomplete information, file an amended return with the correct start date, align the activity code, and comply with local supplemental fee assessments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (INVIMA) and the local municipal authority for alcoholic beverage distribution; Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio for consumer and sanitary surveillance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Bebidas Alcohólicas para Almacenamiento y Distribución de Cerveza Artesanal

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) or the municipal environmental authority (Secretaría de Ambiente) with jurisdiction over the craft brewing and warehouse site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Environmental Management Plan Registration (Plan de Manejo Ambiental Simplificado) applicable to microbreweries with installed capacity below 1,000 liters per day.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Resolution 0631 de 2015 for wastewater discharges into public sewers (BOD5 ≤ 5.0 mg/L, COD ≤ 8.0 mg/L, TSS ≤ 2.0 mg/L, pH 6.0–9.0); air quality and VOC emission limits in accordance with Resolution 2254 de 2017; mandatory solid waste segregation of spent grain, broken glass, and organic waste under Decree 2981 del 2013.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos (fire department) certifying extinguisher distribution, evacuation routes, and structural fire resistance; structural load inspection certificate from the municipal planning office for the keg cold-storage area; occupational health clearance under Resolution 0312 de 2019 (SGSST), including hazard assessment, training records, and personal protective equipment for warehouse operators.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - National Tax and Customs Authority of Colombia; e-services portal MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicios y Control Automatizado) at https://muisca.dian.gov.co; official site https://www.dian.gov.co; single foreign-trade window VUCE at https://vuce.gov.co.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia, acting through the official foreign exchange market intermediaries registered with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia; the Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público defines monetary and FX policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including profit remittances by foreign investors, provided the underlying foreign investment is correctly registered with Banco de la República through the authorized intermediary. Capital-account inflows, in particular paid-in capital increases for a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) owned by non-residents, must be channelled through the exchange market and formalized via the relevant exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio) no later than five business days after the funds are cleared or deposited. Repatriation of dividends and capital reduction proceeds is generally permissible, but the exporter/distributor must evidence the source of funds, payment of Colombian corporate income tax, and compliance with the foreign investment registration. No quantitative convertibility restrictions are applied on registered trade operations; however, unregistered capital may face blockage, fines, or reinvestment treatment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombian exporters must channel export proceeds through the controlled exchange market. For the craft beer wholesale distribution scope, the payment terms for goods must normally be completed within twelve months from the date of the export customs declaration; longer terms require advance authorization. Upon collection, the full export invoice amount must be received through a local bank or authorized FX intermediary within five business days of crediting, and an exchange declaration must be lodged. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio obliging the exporter to sell the foreign currency to Banco de la República; the exporter may credit a lawful foreign-currency deposit account in Colombia. Nonetheless, the proceeds cannot be retained offshore or liquidated outside the regulated Colombian system unless a specific exemption applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (corriente en pesos or foreign-currency account) / Capital Escrow Account for paid-in capital

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to limited viability as a primary clearing rail. Offshore digital EMI institutions cannot hold settlement accounts with Banco de la República, cannot access the Colombian CUD/Cenit clearing system, and are not recognized as credit institutions or authorized FX intermediaries. They may only operate as auxiliary technology vendors with a supervised local bank partner under the simplified digital onboarding framework of Law 1735 of 2014 (SEDPES). For corporate treasury purposes, all inbound and outbound foreign-currency flows must still settle through a licensed Colombian bank or FX intermediary; offshore EMI balances cannot legally receive export proceeds without being routed through a local authorized FX intermediary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated S.A.S. with non-resident shareholders, the legal representative, and in practice the ultimate beneficial owner, must be identified through KYC and AML checks. Tier-1 Colombian banks generally require an in-person interview with the legal representative and, where applicable, the beneficial owner, although some allow a remotely witnessed video interview followed by apostilled powers-of-attorney and physical verification of documents. Fully remote account opening without any physical presence is not the mainstream practice and is accepted only under enhanced due diligence by the bank's risk committee; therefore, we assume the physical interview or a consular/notarial appearance is mandatory for the principal director or attorney-in-fact before the operational account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident individual or entity without a Colombian NIT and without verifiable source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully apostilled constitutional documents of the S.A.S., certificate of existence and legal representation issued by the Cámara de Comercio, beneficial-ownership declaration, passports or national identity documents of all shareholders, bank references from the home jurisdiction, audited financial statements for the prior two fiscal years, and a source-of-wealth statement with supporting asset and transaction documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection or trade receivable derived from accounts located in offshore low-tax jurisdictions or routed via fintech/cryptocurrency processors lacking regulatory recognition.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements showing the direct source of funds, chain-of-title evidence for each remittance, purchase or supply contracts, foreign investment registration draft, tax residence certificates, and an independent legal opinion explaining the commercial rationale of the routing structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic activity mismatch: the company is registered under wholesale distribution (ISIC 4632) but bank propose expects production; large beer distribution flows with no detectable trade documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid sanitary registration or import/export licenses, brewery supply agreements, distributor agreements, transport contracts, warehouse leases, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, certificates of origin, customs export declarations, and insurance certificates covering cold-chain keg transport.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent inbound/outbound FX flows without matching exchange declarations or improper purpose codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of all Formulario de Declaración de Cambio submitted through the local intermediary, bank reference of the intermediary, trade invoices, customs export/import declarations, and a memorandum of treasury policy showing FX hedging and conversion approvals. The company should also provide monthly reconciliation of the operational foreign-currency account to the export proceeds receivable ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders inject capital by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wire transfer to the S.A.S. Capital Escrow Account at a Colombian Tier-1 bank using purpose code 'Direct investment – subscription of shares' or 'Aumento de capital de sociedad extranjera'. The funds must be received through an authorized bank; the exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio, category 'Inversiones Internacionales') must be filed by the bank within five business days of settlement. Adequate documentation includes the shareholders' capital contribution resolution, amended share register, banking source-of-funds proof, and bank reference letters. Once USD/COP conversion is executed, the bank credits the operational COP account and issues a certificado de movimiento cambiario verifiable by Banco de la República.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for imported kegs, hops, malt, yeast, and packaging materials should be disbursed via SWIFT MT103 from the operational account if the supplier accepts direct transfers; for large contractual deliveries and commercial assurance, the importer may open a documentary letter of credit with SWIFT MT700/MT707 under UCP600. All import-related foreign currency disbursements must be declared as 'Declaración de Cambio por Importaciones de Bienes' within five business days of payment or through the bank's automatic reporting system. Domestic disbursements can use the local CUD/ACH system; SWIFT remains mandatory for cross-border counterparties. The USD or EUR account, if maintained, may direct payment of export-related receivables only through a local authorized FX intermediary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/COP regular forward contracts with an authorized Colombian bank or brokerage
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts on USD/COP traded with a local licensed counterparty
Cross-currency swaps (USD/COP principal and interest exchange) with a supervised financial institution
Vanilla FX options (call/put on USD/COP) executed through Banco de la República-registered intermediaries

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registry renewal and filing of prior-year financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) of the registered domicile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a 10% surcharge on the registry fee plus arrears interest; failure to renew for two consecutive annual cycles may result in administrative strike-off and cancellation of the merchant registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual final beneficiary report (Reporte de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the period established by DIAN (exact date set in the annual DIAN filing calendar) and within 10 business days after any share transfer that changes the ultimate beneficial owner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fine per occurrence calculated in UVT under the Colombian Tax Code, and probable suspension or blockage of commercial registration renewal until the obligation is fulfilled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 8 April and 20 June each year, according to the last two digits of the company NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5% per month on tax due, capped at 100% of the tax; default interest applies, and a minimum penalty of 30 UVT if no tax is due.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting to approve financial statements and, if applicable, appoint or remove statutory audit roles
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following the fiscal year-end (within three months after year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting may enable any shareholder to petition a judicial summoning of the meeting; unresolved failure may also impede the annual commercial registry renewal.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Colombian Law 43 of 1990 and Decree 2420 of 2015, an S.A.S. must appoint a Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) when total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV or gross revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV in the preceding fiscal year, or when the company becomes subject to public-interest, capital-market, or consolidation supervision. Below these thresholds, no independent audit is legally required unless the shareholders' meeting voluntarily decides to appoint one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Colombia (NIIF); medium-sized entities may use NIIF para Pymes, and small entities may apply the simplified microenterprise accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must annually confirm and submit to DIAN the final beneficiary information in the format and period prescribed by the DIAN calendar. Any transfer of shares or other act that modifies beneficial ownership must be reported to DIAN within 10 business days and must be recorded in the Register of Members. Failure to record transfers in the statutory registers may render the transfer ineffective against the company and third parties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – USD 600 per year, depending on the local Chamber of Commerce and corporate service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – USD 5,000 per audit engagement, depending on transaction volume and corporate complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (tax year 2024 onward; Law 2277 of 2022 removed the previously envisioned gradual rate decrease to 32% and fixed the general rate at 35% for Sociedades por Acciones Simplificada and other corporations).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 4632 beverage distribution. Available margin-reducers: 50% of the municipal ICA (Industria y Comercio) tax paid is deductible; 100% deduction for qualifying research, technology, and innovation investments; 50% deduction for renewable energy investments; 20% discount for new-job creation linked to 18–25-year-old employees; other 'rentas exentas' are limited to specific sectors (orange economy, ecotourism, senior employment) and do not apply to craft beer wholesale.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 'Declaración de Renta y Complementarios' for legal entities; filed electronically through the DIAN portal (Muisca – Sistema de Facturación Electrónica y Registro Único Tributario). Monthly withholding returns (Formulario 350) and informational TP returns (Formularios 120/121) are separate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the Form 110 covers the previous calendar fiscal year. Monthly Formulario 350 applies for withholding remittances, including dividend WHT and payments to non-residents.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadlines are fixed each year by DIAN Resolution and depend on the final two digits of the NIT; for fiscal year 2023 the filing window ran from 10 April 2024 through 11 June 2024. The filing due date in subsequent years will similarly fall between April and June following the fiscal year-end, scheduled by the annual DIAN masternomenclature.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) of the filing company and the verifying digit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. supplies the Colombian NIT obtained at formation; the foreign beneficial owner's home-country tax ID never appears in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name ('Razón Social') matching the November 2023/current RUT registration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name registered with the DIAN; transliterations acceptable only when the municipal registry file differs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions, exempt income, and amortized loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. is the entity-level taxpayer; non-resident shareholders do not compute this field on Form 110. Deductions must be causally linked to Colombian-source activities, including cold-chain freight to foreign wholesalers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory rate applied to the taxable base; the box reflects the 35% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entity-level rate; treaty or foreign-tax-credit positions of the shareholders are not taken into account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Renglón 46 – Impuesto sobre la renta a cargo
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income tax before discounts and advance payments; equals Renta Líquida Gravable × Tarifa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-domiciled shareholders cannot offset personal withholding against the S.A.S. corporate tax in this line; only the company's own anticipo and audited retentions are applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net treasury payable after descuentos tributarios (R&D discount, renewable energy discount, ICA deduction), retenciones a título de renta paid, and anticipo adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident legal representatives must ensure cash settlement via DIAN's electronic debit protocols; foreign shareholders cannot assume personal credit relief against the corporate liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 'sanción por extemporaneidad' — 5% of the tax due per month (or fraction) of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due; where no tax is due the sanction is equivalent to 1% of gross income. Late payment interest accrues at the DIAN-published effective daily rate (approximately 2.19% per month in 2024). Filing under false information: 'sanción por inexactitud' of up to 160% of the understated tax. Directors may be jointly liable where the omission is agreed by the governing body.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (Article 245 E.T.) on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders, withheld by the S.A.S. at the time of distribution; dividends paid from non-taxable reserves or the higher taxable surplus bear additional 35% closures, leaving a practical 20% ceiling for the most aggressive distribution structures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority in the current calendar year; (ii) deliver the TRC and a beneficial-ownership statement to the Colombian paying company before the payment date; (iii) the Colombian payer then files the corresponding 'Formato de concepto del beneficiario efectivo' and withholding documentation through Muisca; (iv) the reduced treaty rate is applied at source only when the TRC is presented within the same taxable period — retroactive application requires a 'solicitud de devolución' (Form 150) plus interest forfeiture risks. Colombian DTAs (Spain, Chile, Mexico, Canada, South Korea, Portugal, France, Netherlands, Switzerland, among others) commonly cap dividends at 0%–15%; rate benefits are denied if the shareholder lacks beneficial ownership or real economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic rates: royalties and technical-service fees paid to non-residents — 15% unified base (Law 2277 of 2022 harmonized the prior 10%–30% distortions); pure copyright royalties may remain at 10%; certain know-how/licensing structures face up to 33% withholding where the payor cannot evidence genuine IP ownership or where the payment is treated as profit distribution. Interest paid abroad: 15% for external credit channeled through regulated financial intermediaries; 20% for interest to other foreign creditors and shareholders-loans. Treaty rates generally compress both to 5%–15%, subject to the limitation-on-benefits and beneficial-ownership tests.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: COP 7,059,750,000 (150,000 UVT × COP 47,065 UVT value for tax year 2024) of prior-year gross income is the minimum threshold for mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; however, any taxpayer with related-party cross-border transactions must possess contemporaneous TP analysis, and DIAN may require the Form 120/121 informational return when the taxpayer crosses a lower de minimis transaction threshold or operates with tax-haven counterparties. Transfer-pricing scrutiny is heightened for a distribution S.A.S. purchasing Keg inventory from a related foreign brewer or selling to related foreign wholesalers.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) — preferred for commodity-like keg transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not impose a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation decree, but the DIAN applies the economic-substance/substance-over-form doctrine through Article 124 E.T. and the general anti-abuse concept inserted by Law 2277 of 2022. The S.A.S. must demonstrate real operational presence: leased cold-storage, employed logistics staff, purchase orders, delivery invoices, and insurance — a mere flow-through issuing invoices for foreign principals will be recharacterized, its intercompany management fees disallowed, and its export pricing reassessed. A second application of substance arises under Colombian DTAs: treaty benefits are denied where the receiving entity is a pure mailbox entity lacking 'beneficial ownership'.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating export revenues or overstating deductible costs by issuing fictitious Keg-purchase invoices, double-billing cold-chain freight, or misclassifying payments to the foreign parent as deductible royalties rather than equity distributions. Also includes failure to file Form 110 entirely while the S.A.S. maintained operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN 'sanción por inexactitud' of 100%–160% of the understated tax; late interest at the monthly effective rate (≈2.19% per month); criminal sanction under Article 434 of the Código Penal: 48–108 months imprisonment and a fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax if the amount exceeds the legal threshold, which is easily attained by a year of unreported craft-bear exports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the legal representative sign the Form 110; knowingly false filing opens personal criminal liability, and the corporate veil of the S.A.S. may be pierced under Article 30 of Law 1258 of 2008 — the director's personal assets are attachable for the tax debt, travel bans ('salida del país') may be ordered during criminal proceedings, and civil restitution with prison time applies in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Colombian S.A.S. as a conduit: invoicing related-party supply chains without holding inventory risk, appointing a nominee director abroad, no local payroll, and accumulating profits distributed to a low-tax jurisdiction treaty resident without commercial activity in Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN recharacterization of all related-party transactions at arm's length; disallowance of every management fee, interest, and royalty paid to the foreign shareholder; reclassification of these distributions as dividends subject to the 35% corporate-level closure and 10% non-resident dividend WHT; possible aggregate penalty of 160%. Treaty benefits are denied retroactively with interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who lend their name to the conduit are personally liable for the S.A.S. tax obligations if found to be 'administradores de hecho' — their personal assets are subject to seizure; criminal cooperation charges apply where the director knowingly signed documentation for a sham company designed to evade tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering through Cross-Border Keg Sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving cash deposits into Colombian bank accounts from unknown third parties, invoicing below-market prices to shell distributors, structured swift-wire transfers below reporting thresholds, or failure to identify the beneficial owner of the S.A.S. in the RUT when suspicious movements appear under the SARLAFT framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money-laundering crime under Article 323 of the Código Penal: 128–360 months imprisonment (roughly 10–30 years) and a fine equivalent to 1,500–50,000 times the current legal minimum wage; the competent authority ('Fiscalía' and UIAF) may order the extinction of domain over the S.A.S. shares, cold-storage inventory, and distribution fleet, even before a final criminal conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally prosecuted when they execute or authorize suspicious transfers; civil confiscation of personal assets proceeds in parallel; travel bans and freezing of personal bank accounts accompany the criminal process; a director's lack of awareness is no defense once they sign the suspicious wire instructions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Intentional Insolvency / Diverting Corporate Assets to Shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: In the period preceding DIAN collection, transferring keg inventory, real-estate storage, or cash to the non-resident parent below market, issuing shareholder loans to the parent, or favoring one foreign creditor over the DIAN — a fraud upon the tax creditor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The 'acción pauliana' and Colombian insolvency law (Ley 1116 de 2006) allow voiding of such preferential transfers; the DIAN becomes revocable creditor; additional sanction for fraudulent insolvency (Código Penal Article 250): 6–12 years imprisonment; the S.A.S. is liquidated with the DIAN as a preferred claim.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the board and the legal representative who orchestrated the asset-stripping are jointly and severally liable for the full tax claim; they face travel restrictions until the treasury is restored, banking prohibitions, and criminal imprisonment where the scheme involved forged invoices or simulated contracts.
